hints: Define a continuous residual such as $f(x)=\cot(x/2)-3x$ and evaluate it in radians at both endpoints.
Show that the two residuals have opposite signs, then invoke continuity to locate the root between $0.5$ and $1$.
walkthrough:
Conclude the root location:
Since $f(x)$ is continuous on $[0.5, 1]$ and changes sign between $x = 0.5$ ($f(0.5) > 0$) and $x = 1$ ($f(1) < 0$), the root $\alpha$ lies strictly between $0.5$ and $1$.

ai_rubric.Numerical Root Bracketing: Endpoint evaluations at 0.5 and 1 establish the sign change or ordering. Completes the argument with values and a sign/inequality change, e.g. $3.92>1.5$, $1.83<3$, or residuals $2.42>0$, $-1.17<0$. Substitution at $x=0.5$, $\cot(0.25)=3.92>1.5$; at $x=1$, $\cot(0.5)=1.83<3$.

hints: If the iteration converges, both $x_n$ and $x_{n+1}$ tend to the same limit; call it $x$.
Set $x=\frac13\left(x+4\tan^{-1}\!\frac1{3x}\right)$ and rearrange to isolate the inverse tangent.
Convert the resulting relation involving $\tan(x/2)$ into $\cot(x/2)=3x$; the unique root in $(0,\pi)$ is therefore $\alpha$.
walkthrough:
Assume the iterative formula converges to a limit $x$:
$$x = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(x + 4\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{3x}\right)\right)$$

Take the tangent of both sides:
$$\tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{3x}$$

Take the reciprocal of both sides to obtain the original equation:
$$\cot\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) = 3x$$
Since this is the equation whose root in $(0, \pi)$ is $\alpha$, the sequence converges to $\alpha$.

ai_rubric.Forming and Testing Fixed-Point Rearrang: Gives $x=\frac13[x+4\tan^{-1}(1/(3x))]$. Rearranges to the given equation $\cot(x/2)=3x$. At convergence, $x=\frac13[x+4\tan^{-1}(1/(3x))]$, which rearranges to $\cot(x/2)=3x$.

hints: Choose a starting value in the bracket from part (a) and substitute it into the given iteration, using radians.
Feed each new value back into the formula and record every iterate to $4$ decimal places.
Continue until successive iterates agree sufficiently to justify rounding the limiting value to $2$ decimal places.
walkthrough:
Start with $x_1 = 0.75$ and compute subsequent iterations to 4 decimal places in radians:
$$x_2 = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(0.75 + 4\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{3(0.75)}\right)\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}(0.75 + 4(0.418224)) = 0.8076$$

Round the final answer correct to 2 decimal places:
$$\alpha = 0.79$$

ai_rubric.Fixed-Point Iteration: Substitution into $\alpha$ gives consecutive iterates $0.79\to0.785\to0.795$, converging to $\alpha=0.79$.
